what: Natera makes genetic tests from blood samples. Its main products screen pregnancies for chromosomal conditions, test transplanted organs for rejection, and detect traces of tumour DNA in cancer patients after surgery.
customers: Obstetricians, oncologists and transplant centres, with testing paid for by insurers and health systems.
money: molecular residual disease testing after cancer treatment
moat: A tumour-informed test built from each patient's own cancer, backed by clinical evidence and insurer coverage decisions that took years to win.
risks: It still loses money at the operating line
Insurer reimbursement decisions determine whether tests get paid for
Competitors are launching similar cancer monitoring tests
The shares trade at a very high multiple of revenue
opportunities: Revenue grew about 36% last year and about 41% a year over three years
Signatera volumes keep rising as oncologists adopt residual disease testing
Cash of about $1.1 billion against little debt funds the growth
watch: Signatera test volumes and gross margin as the mix shifts to oncology.
